memo.verdict: Park. Neutral on the shares at SEK 187.2 (2026-09-23); bullish on the business. Two triggers to progress: a price below about SEK 150 on the modal path (about SEK 165 if the Q3 report on 15 October 2026 and the successor announcement together make the multiple's hold probable rather than possible; about SEK 140 under the adverse drop-through), or, at any price near today's, a committed leverage step toward 2.0x net debt to EBITDA under a named successor with the deal discipline intact, which moves the modal path to the leverage branch that clears the bar. Conviction medium on the operating case and medium on the valuation call. The park is argued on the return, not gated: no D or F sits on management, business quality, predictability or trackability. Thesis in one line: OEM International is the right company under a new owner doing the right thing, at a price that has already paid for it. Modal total shareholder return about 3 percent a year over eighteen months and about 7 percent a year over three years against the framework's 20 percent bar.
case: - The change is internal, broad and already acting. EQT took control in February 2025; the founding families sold about 75 percent of their holdings at SEK 110, the largest insider sale in 43 years listed. New chairman, six of seven directors, Deputy CEO, CFO; the chief executive of 24 years leaves by 31 December 2026 with no successor named. The mandate widened to product-owning niches, a dedicated acquisition team was set up in 2025, and seven deals in the twelve months to July 2026 added SEK 476m of annual sales against about 3 percent a year of acquired growth over 2015 to 2024 (six in the first half of 2026 against one in the first half of 2025; SEK 275m of cash in the first half of FY2026 against SEK 108m in all of FY2025). Capital allocation shifted from paying 53 to 54 percent of cash flow as dividends and letting cash build to SEK 603m at end-2025 toward deploying it. Net debt to EBITDA moved from -0.81x to -0.13x.

- A cyclical recovery arrived at the same time and is not the change's doing: organic growth 1 percent Q4 2025, 5 percent Q1 2026, 8 percent Q2 2026; orders +23 percent; backlog +34 percent giving visibility into the first half of 2027; Eurozone manufacturing PMI 52.7 in August 2026; Finland organic +23 percent after a multi-year downturn. Construction in Sweden and Finland "weak and depressed", Swedish housing starts not recovered, German industrial production down 1.6 percent sequentially in July 2026, Rest of Europe organic -2 percent; the Finnish rebound "appears disconnected from underlying Eurozone manufacturing PMI trends", so restocking is possible. About twelve months of visibility, not the two-plus years a 'Demand Inflection' needs.

- The change has travelled the whole 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain for its first step: owner (resources), mandate and hires (choices), deals (actions), acquired growth 9 percent of sales in Q2 2026 (operating metrics), EBITA +37 percent and EPS +31 percent (financial statements), consensus EPS +10 percent over six months (estimates). The next step, leverage toward SEK 2,000m of capacity at 2.0x under a successor who keeps the cadence, is at the first two layers only.
counter_case: The sell-side's case in its strongest form: this is a proven compounder at the start of its second engine. Historically superior organic growth (7.0 percent a year over 2021 to 2025 against Addtech flat), cash conversion of 66 percent of EBITA over five years, a 30.7 percent return on capital employed, a balance sheet that funds SEK 2,000m of deals at 2.0x net debt to EBITDA without equity, a sponsor whose playbook at Beijer Ref accelerated both acquisitions and organic growth, and a consensus that by construction leaves unsigned deals out, so every deal signed is an upgrade. At 15 percent-plus EBITA growth over the cycle, 27.8x 2026e EV/EBITA is the right multiple (DNB Carnegie's SEK 200), RedEye's fair-value range runs to SEK 235, DNB Carnegie's leverage case is 30 percent annual EBITA growth, and 29x is not a de-rating risk but the level a compounder holds while it compounds; the proven compounders' premium of 22x against 17x has held for five years. The evidence: the Q2 2026 beat of 9 percent on EBITA, the 34 percent backlog rise, seven deals, the peers' premium holding. On the 'Investment Case' rating specifically: the record is marking the case down for price alone; at 10 percent a year on the 24-month-forward figure, today's 29.0x is about 22x on the earnings of 2029, where the proven compounders trade, so a holder who ignores the multiple for three years owns a compounder at a compounder's price by the end. On the 'Foundations': they are being hollowed out while the near-term numbers look best; management quality through the dual chief-executive and CFO change is "medium plausibility"; cultural dilution under EQT is the single largest risk to a decentralised, family-like model whose senior team dates from the 1980s; the risks research's verdict is FALSE FRIEND, near-term deal and margin momentum masking structural decay, with the sponsor's shorter horizon, the 200 percent variable cap with no clawback, turnover up to 13 percent, earn-outs written back from SEK 46.5m to SEK 9.8m and no hedging on 80 percent of foreign-currency purchases as the signs; the 2014 to 2024 record belongs to a regime being replaced and the 2026 numbers are its last plus a cycle. On the setup: it is really 'Demand Inflection' wearing corporate-change clothes; the internal change has produced 9 percent of acquired growth at a normal margin while the organic acceleration from 1 to 8 percent, the 23 percent order growth, the 34 percent backlog and a 23 percent Finnish recovery are what moved the estimates and the price; when the cycle rolls over the multiple goes with it whatever EQT does.

The record's response. It concedes most of the operating argument: the business is of the quality claimed, unsigned deals will enter consensus, the leverage branch if taken at the old discipline justifies the multiple and returns about 26 percent a year, and the earnings will grow into the multiple. It holds its view because the return at this price rests on the multiple holding; the multiple holding rests on two plausible conditions with joint odds of about 40 percent; and the branch that would justify the multiple outright is possible not modal, since SEK 275m was deployed in the first half of 2026 against SEK 2,000m of capacity, deal sizes are SEK 30m to 250m of sales, the person who would execute it is unnamed, the stated ceiling of debt-to-equity under 100 percent has never been approached, and the forty-year habit is caution. A 40 percent branch at 10.5 percent a year and a 60 percent branch at about -2 percent a year is a modal 3 percent against a bar of 20; a case that returns a D when everything goes right on the operations is a case to own at a different price. On the Foundations it holds B because the evidence of decay is absent so far (organic growth 1 to 8 percent in three quarters; margin up 220 basis points; return on equity back at the 25 percent floor; defaults 0.01 percent of sales) and the subsidiary layer, where the culture lives, is untouched; the counter-case would win on a successor from outside the model with a platform-deal brief or two or more division-head departures within a year, both on the monitoring table. On the setup it holds 'Major Corporate Change' because the durable part of the case is the internal change (the cadence and the balance sheet will be there in FY2028 whether or not the PMI is above 50, and the modelled return rests on about 8 percent acquired growth more than on 5 to 6 percent organic), while conceding the counter-case is right on the price: the multiple has been paid for the cycle as much as the change, which is why the modal return is thin and why a de-rating on a soft quarter is the risk that binds. The counter-case does not change the setup; it changes what to pay for it. The counter-case is a reason to own the business at about SEK 150, or at SEK 187 on the day leverage is committed under a named successor; not a reason to own it at SEK 187 on the hope that it will be.
triggers: - Progress triggers: a price below about SEK 150 on the modal path (about SEK 165 if the Q3 report on 15 October 2026 and the successor announcement together make the multiple's hold probable; about SEK 140 under the adverse drop-through; about SEK 132 on the three-year view); or a committed leverage step toward 2.0x under a named successor with deal discipline intact, at any price near today's.

- The successor: unnamed; contract ends 31 December 2026 at the latest. Alarm: no announcement by 31 December 2026. Invalidate: departures of two or more division heads within a year of the change. Up if a successor from outside the model brings a platform-deal brief with the discipline intact; the record's modal case is a successor named by year-end who keeps the cadence.

- The acquisition cadence: current seven deals in twelve months, six in the first half of 2026; modal about eight a year of SEK 30m to 250m of sales at mid-to-high single-digit EBITA multiples. Alarm: fewer than four deals in a year, or any deal above 7x EBITA. Invalidate: a large deal above 10x EBITA on debt. A stated leverage target or a platform deal above SEK 500m of sales moves the modal path to the leverage branch. Multiples paid in 2026 are not disclosed in the files; earn-out write-backs (SEK 46.5m to SEK 9.8m) are the discipline signal to watch. Return on capital employed: current 30.7 percent (2025); modal 25 to 30 percent; alarm below 25 percent; invalidate below 20 percent.

- Organic growth and the cycle: current 8 percent (Q2 2026), PMI 52.7 (August 2026); modal 5 to 6 percent over the cycle. Alarm: below 5 percent for two quarters, or the PMI back below 50. Invalidate: below 1 percent sustained. The Q3 print on 15 October 2026 is the first test of the backlog against a multiple that expects no softness; the third quarter is seasonally the softest. Whether the Finnish +23 percent is end demand or restocking is unresolved. Construction in Sweden and Finland and its spread into industrial manufacturing; German industrial weakness.

- The EBITA margin: current 15.4 percent (Q2 2026); modal 16 percent held; alarm below 14 percent for a quarter without a currency explanation; invalidate below 12 percent for two quarters. Brokers see 17.7 to 18.3 percent EBITDA margin on their basis; the record holds product-owning integration and central costs against the mix gain.

- The multiple: current 28.75x to 30.4x; modal 26.2x blended; alarm a de-rating below 24.3x with earnings intact, which is the buying level, not the selling one. The multiple falls first on a Q3 miss.
